newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac back stable franc-mark exchange rate.
newsitem.headline: Chirac back stable franc-mark exchange rate.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said after talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Saturday that he supported a stable franc-mark exchange rate.

In a brief statement to reporters after the two men met in the southwestern French town of Perigueux, Chirac said: "I confirmed the French position on the stable relationship between the franc and the mark, as the prime minister (Alain Juppe) said the other day in the National Assembly."

It was the first time Chirac had spoken out on the monetary issue since ex-president Valery Giscard d'Estaing stirred controversy by calling for a depreciation of the franc to boost economic growth and combat record unemployment in France.
Kohl said he did not wish to interfere in France's domestic politics but he was very pleased to hear that France intended to meet the criteria for launching a single European currency in 1999.
"I am happy that the criteria (for monetary union) have once again been confirmed here," Kohl said.

The chancellor said he was convinced European economic and monetary union was of crucial important, both in giving the European Union strength in relation to the dollar and other currencies and in creating jobs in Europe.
